title: Add experimental .NET Web export support using static LibGodot
body:
Based on and preserving authorship from #118976 by @NoctemCat. This rebases the static LibGodot approach onto current `master` and refines the Web export integration.

## What changed

- Adds experimental .NET Web export support using the standard .NET browser-wasm runtime and a statically linked LibGodot.
- Supports threaded and non-threaded Web templates, C# ↔ JavaScript interop, AOT, cryptography, and `HttpClient`.
- Packages the static engine, Emscripten configuration, JavaScript libraries, and pre/post-JS hooks in the Web template.
- Adds the corresponding Godot .NET SDK browser props/targets and managed/native bridge.
- Preserves the normal Web export lifecycle by extracting only the internal `libgodot` payload before export plugins run, then extracting regular HTML/JS template files in their established phase.
- Fixes the Web/macOS build-output embedding condition after rebasing.
- Updates the implementation for current `master`, including the current export notification API and Python 3.9 compatibility.

## Why

Godot 4 currently rejects C# Web exports. The .NET browser-wasm toolchain needs to own the final Emscripten link, while Godot normally produces a complete WebAssembly executable itself. Building Godot as a static library lets the .NET SDK link the managed application, .NET runtime, and engine into one WebAssembly module.

## Validation

- Built a macOS .NET editor and generated/packaged the matching Godot .NET SDK.
- Built non-threaded static LibGodot Web debug template.
- Built threaded static LibGodot Web debug template with `proxy_to_pthread=yes`.
- Exported a C# test project with both templates.
- Ran both exports in Chromium.
- Verified managed constructors and `_Ready`, Variant marshalling, cryptography, `HttpClient`, JavaScript imports/exports, and the expected JavaScript → C# return value.
- Verified worker-thread entry and exit in the threaded export under COOP/COEP isolation headers.
- Ran `git diff --check`, Python compile checks, and XML validation for the SDK props/targets.

## Current limitations

- Requires Emscripten 3.1.56 until the .NET runtime toolchain moves forward.
- Dynamic GDExtensions are not supported in C# Web exports.
- Godot LTO is not supported for this static library path.
- Exports are slower because every export performs the final native WebAssembly link.
- Threaded exports require cross-origin isolation and inherit .NET browser threading/interop limitations.
- Threaded exports are incompatible with WebXR for the same reason as `proxy_to_pthread`.

This remains experimental and is intentionally submitted as a draft.
